name: Philips Hue Smart Plug (EU)

radios.note: Bluetooth for direct app control; Zigbee (2.4 GHz) to the Hue Bridge. No Wi-Fi.

matter.note: No Matter certification found for the plug itself. Hue says products connected to a Hue Bridge are exposed to Matter by the Bridge.

apple_home.note: Apple Home is linked from the Hue app with a Hue Bridge. Hue's EU product pages are inconsistent about listing Apple Home.

google_home.note: The German product page says voice control with Google Assistant needs a Hue Bridge.

alexa.note: The German product page says voice control with Alexa needs a Hue Bridge.

smartthings.note: The Hue Bridge page lists Samsung SmartThings compatibility. That page is the US one; we assume the EU Bridge behaves the same.

home_assistant.note: Official Hue integration controls devices connected to a Hue Bridge.

hubRequired.note: Basic control works over Bluetooth from the Hue app; the Hue Bridge is needed for voice assistants, ecosystems and remote access.

localControl.note: Bluetooth control without a bridge or Wi-Fi; the Hue Bridge also offers a local API used by Home Assistant.

energyMonitoring.note: Hue's pages describe on/off switching only and list no metering, but none says explicitly that it is absent.

maxLoadWatts.note: Hue support gives 2300 W for mainland Europe (220–240 V). The UK version has a different rating.

summary: The EU Philips Hue Smart Plug talks Bluetooth to the Hue app for basic on/off, with no Wi-Fi. Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa, SmartThings and Home Assistant all need a Hue Bridge; the plug joins it over Zigbee, and the Bridge also exposes it to Matter platforms. It fits 220–240 V mainland European sockets and is rated 2300 W. Hue doesn't list energy metering.
caveats: Voice assistants, ecosystems and remote access all need a Hue Bridge.
Bluetooth-only setups can't use Matter; the Bridge is what exposes the plug to Matter.
Rated 2300 W in mainland Europe, below the 3680 W of many 16 A Schuko plugs.
